claim: The 10-year US Treasury real (TIPS) yield (DFII10) stood at 2.55% as of 2026-09-10, up from 2.43% on 2026-09-04, and implies a 10-year breakeven inflation rate of approximately 2.40 percentage points on 2026-09-10 (4.95% nominal minus 2.55% real).
stance_target: pinning the present real-rate environment with dates, since real yield matters more than nominal for equity-duration arguments
scope_conditions: US TIPS market, daily observations, not seasonally adjusted

claim: In the observed early-September 2026 window, the real 10-year yield rose by about 12 basis points while the nominal 10-year yield rose by about 17 basis points over the same days, indicating the move was predominantly a real-rate (discount-rate) shift rather than a shift in inflation expectations.
stance_target: distinguishing a real-rate/pure-discounting shock from an inflation-expectations shock, relevant to which component should pass through to equity valuations per Gormsen & Lazarus
scope_conditions: US Treasury and TIPS markets, 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-10
